key_insight: Mac-Diff is a conditional diffusion model that uses locality-aware cross-modal attention to generate diverse, realistic conformational ensembles for unseen proteins, capturing both dynamic flexibility and structural heterogeneity.
problem_solved: Overcomes the limitation of single-structure protein predictors by efficiently generating diverse, physically plausible conformational ensembles that reflect protein dynamics and structural heterogeneity.
method: Conditional diffusion generative model (Mac-Diff) that samples ensembles conditioned on input modalities (e.g., sequence and structural cues).
Locality-aware modal alignment via cross-modal attention enforces local correspondence between modalities, improving realistic local structural variation.
Training and sampling strategies emphasize ensemble diversity and fidelity to known biophysical metrics, producing broader coverage than deterministic predictors.
impact: Provides ML practitioners a scalable generative framework for modeling protein dynamics and producing diverse candidate structures useful for drug design, functional inference, and improved downstream learning. Demonstrates locality-aware attention as a powerful pattern for aligning modalities in generative models.
visual_elements: Architecture schematic: conditional diffusion pipeline with locality-aware cross-modal attention blocks.
Overlay visualization: multiple sampled conformations vs a single predicted structure to show gained diversity.
Attention heatmaps: locality-aware alignment between sequence/feature positions and structural coordinates.
Performance charts: diversity and accuracy metrics (ensemble coverage, RMSD, energy) comparing Mac-Diff to baselines.
paper_title: Conditional diffusion with locality-aware modal alignment for generating diverse protein conformational ensembles
paper_authors: Baoli Wang, Chenglin Wang, Jingyang Chen, Danlin Liu, Changzhi Sun
